subject: Sprint 2 correctness and performance repairs (S2-R-04, S2-R-03, S1-R-16), the post-repair real-corpus re-measurement, and the project-memory updates describing them
summary: All three repairs under review are correct and independently reproduced, not merely asserted. Overlapping roots claim each file exactly once, deterministically, order-independently, with the condition printed to stderr on every sync. A sync performs exactly one discovery pass while cursor semantics, skip-and-report, tombstone-not-purge and every CLI counter are preserved. The golden-baseline assertion demonstrably fails on a simulated ranking regression, including the subtlest one-place demotion its tolerance claims to catch, and on a tampered or truncated baseline document. The reviewer re-ran a clean full sync of the real corpus under /usr/bin/time -v and reproduced both the corpus shape (1,213 items, 12,699 chunks, 21,020,672 bytes) and the post-repair performance figures within 3% on every metric, and re-derived discovery with and without the claiming rule to reproduce both the pre-repair git-ignored counter of 300 and the post-repair 14 from the same corpus. A repository-wide leak scan over all 75 tracked files passes. No Critical or High finding survived verification. Eight advisories remain: absolute host paths persist in 14 unpushed commits and one path shape is already published; a discovery-time read failure tombstones a live item with no counter and misreports it as deleted; a scoped sync loses overlap-region files to no counter; and the customer-facing evidence report contradicts itself on the git-ignored counter.

readiness.criterion: S2-R-04 repaired: one file is claimed by exactly one deterministic root, and the nested-root condition is operator-visible
readiness.basis: Reviewer probe over two overlapping roots: 3 on-disk files yield 3 objects resolving to 3 distinct files; the deepest root wins; the claim is stable across repeated passes and identical under reversed declaration order; the parent correctly reclaims when the child's include no longer matches; identical-path roots resolve by name tie-break. The reviewer's own full real-corpus sync printed 'nested roots detected (deepest matching root claims overlaps): jobsearch -> agent-in-a-box, pr-business -> pr-research' to stderr. In-repo regression tests exist at tests/test_local_connector.py:539 and :576.

readiness.criterion: S2-R-03 repaired: exactly one discovery pass per sync, with cursor semantics, skip-and-report, tombstoning and CLI counters unchanged
readiness.basis: Instrumented six-pass sync over an eight-candidate corpus counted discover_report=1, Path.rglob=1 and git check-ignore subprocesses=1 per pass; hashing is once per candidate in discovery plus once per changed object in fetch (pass 1: 12 = 6 + 6; pass 2 unchanged: 7 = 6 + 1). Cursor semantics, the unchanged denominator, tombstone-not-purge (tombstone=1 with the row retained), the token-tripwire's re-report-every-pass behaviour and the git_ignored / unhandled_formats counters all reproduce across every pass. tests/test_cli.py:185-221 asserts invocation_count == 1 independently.

readiness.basis: Control run passes (exit 0, 1 passed). A mutant retriever reversing the provider's final order fails (exit 1, 'operational-01 lost its top-10 citation entirely'). Demoting exactly one of the twenty questions from rank 1 to rank 2 also fails (exit 1, 'hit_at_1 drifted ... observed 0.5500, recorded 0.6000, tolerance 0.01'). Redirecting BASELINE_DOC_PATH to a copy edited to 80.0% fails ('observed 0.6000, recorded 0.8000'), proving the gate reads the document live; deleting the bullet fails with the explicit 'Could not parse the Baseline section' assertion rather than skipping.

readiness.criterion: Re-measured corpus counts are reproducible from the run, and the change in the git-ignored counter is explained
readiness.basis: Read-only re-derivation from .lee-kb/real-corpus.sqlite reproduces 1,213 live items, 0 tombstoned, 12,699 chunks, 15 roots, every per-root row of the Corpus Shape table, 21,020,672 bytes on disk, 13 canonical / 1,200 derived and 1,211 curated / 2 model_produced. An independent clean full re-sync by the reviewer reproduced the same shape from scratch. Re-deriving discovery over the 15 real roots with the claiming rule active gives indexable=1213, git_ignored=14, git_unresolved=5, unhandled={}; bypassing claiming gives indexable=1213, git_ignored=300 — reproducing both the pre-repair and post-repair counters from the same corpus and confirming the repair changed only the diagnostic.

findings.location: git history: playbooks/sprint_02_p1_real_corpus_parity.yaml at commits 9cca4df, 4e9b989, 7e74e56, b980cdd; .agent-orch-scratch/.agent-orch-scratch-root.json at 8 commits from fc757f4 to 4e9b989; context.md at 95f63c9 and earlier
findings.problem: S2-R-01, S2-R-02 and S2-R-12 sanitized the working tree by rewriting files forward; the absolute host paths they removed are still present in the commits. Four commits carry the absolute path to the private corpus configuration and the factory workspace root, and eight carry the absolute path of this checkout. The remote github.com/leebase/lee-kb is at 95f63c9, an ancestor of local HEAD, so those 14 commits are unpushed and publish verbatim on the first git push. A third path shape -- a /Volumes mount recorded as the working directory in context.md -- is already published, being present at 95f63c9 itself and at two earlier remote commits. Project memory records the disclosure class as repaired. Severity is Medium rather than High: the mission's at-least-High rule is scoped to tracked files and the tracked-file scan passes cleanly; the disclosed material is filesystem layout plus the account name lee, which this repository already publishes in README.md, src/lee_kb/main.py:61 and 39 occurrences of lee@leebase.com, with no credential, document content or in-corpus document path; and the previous review rated this identical disclosure in a tracked file of a live public repository (S2-R-02) as Medium.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the 14 unpushed commits before the first push -- squash them into a sanitized set, or run git filter-repo to drop .agent-orch-scratch and rewrite the playbook blob -- then re-verify with a scan over git rev-list --all. The already-published /Volumes path cannot be recalled by a rewrite, so decide explicitly whether it matters. Extend the repository-wide scan rule at skills/documentation.md:50 so it walks every reachable tree, not only the checkout.

findings.problem: In a scoped sync (lee-kb sync local_files <root>), _claiming_root still consults every configured root, so a file inside an overlap region is skipped by the root being synced and never scanned by the claiming root, which is out of scope for that pass. It lands in no counter. Reproduced: two overlapping roots over a three-file tree, discover_report(root_name='parent') returns 1 object while the other 2 files -- both matched by the parent root's own include patterns -- are neither indexed nor counted (git_ignored=0, unhandled_formats={}). This contradicts the DiscoveryReport docstring at local_files.py:514 ('accounted for in exactly one place') and the SyncSummary docstring at main.py:84-85 ('must never disappear without a count'). The stderr nested-root notice tells the operator overlaps exist, not that this pass lost files to one.
findings.proposed_fix: Count claim-losses in DiscoveryReport (for example claimed_by_other_root) and print the segment in the sync summary line, or -- when root_name is set and the claiming root is outside the requested scope -- let the requested root claim the file for that pass. Add a scoped-sync regression test over two overlapping roots asserting every on-disk candidate is either indexed or counted.

findings.location: src/lee_kb/connectors/local_files.py:702-707 (discover_report ConnectorReadError handler); src/lee_kb/main.py:199-209 (_changes_from_objects deletion diff) and :249-255 (tombstone_item)
findings.problem: An already-indexed document that becomes temporarily unreadable is removed from the searchable projection with no counter and is misreported to the operator as a deletion. discover_report() catches ConnectorReadError from _describe and continues without incrementing anything; _changes_from_objects then sees the id missing from the current set and emits DELETED; _sync_connector tombstones the item and drops its cursor entry. Reproduced: chmod 000 on one indexed file of a six-document corpus makes the next pass print '0 created, 0 updated, 1 deleted, 3 unchanged' with skipped=0 and no counter moving for the unreadable file; the item is tombstoned and returns as '1 created' on the following readable pass. Pre-existing -- the pre-repair list_changes/discover path behaved identically -- so S2-R-03 did not introduce it, and the S1-R-10 fetch-time skip-and-report guard sits downstream of the hole and never sees the object. Severity is Medium rather than High: nothing is destroyed (the source remains authoritative, the item is tombstoned rather than purged so receipts stay resolvable, and the projection self-heals on the next readable sync), and the trigger is an unreadable file rather than normal use; S1-R-10 was rated High because a read failure aborted the entire sync, which this does not.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a read_failures counter to DiscoveryReport and SyncSummary, increment it where the ConnectorReadError is currently swallowed, print it in the sync summary line, and exclude read-failed source_object_ids from the DELETED diff so a transient permission or I/O error cannot tombstone a live item. Add a sync test covering an already-indexed file that becomes unreadable.

findings.problem: The customer-facing measurement artifact states two different values for the same post-repair counter and carries two statements the same edit invalidated. 'What Was Not Indexed' (:50) and Parity Gaps (:111) both present 300 git-ignored as this run's CLI counter, while Performance (:94) and the S2-R-04 note (:113) say 14. The reviewer's own independent clean full re-sync prints '14 git-ignored', so 14 is current and :50 and :111 are stale pre-repair text. Recommended Next Actions #4 (:122) still tells the reader to treat sync wall-clock ~5m20s and peak memory ~4.5 GiB as the baseline, in a document whose Performance table now records 2:51.18. Recommended Next Actions #5 (:123) still reads 'No correctness defects were found in this pass' in a document that now records three repaired defects.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-scope :50 and :111 to the pre-repair run or update them to 14 with a pointer to the Performance explanation; update Recommended Next Actions #4 to the post-repair baseline; re-word #5 so it refers to the original measurement pass rather than the document as a whole.

findings.problem: Three places in project memory restate the pre-repair peak resident set size as '~4.48 GiB'. 4,585,924 KB is 4.373 GiB. Commit 19b8d4d corrected exactly this parenthetical inside evidence/real-corpus-parity-report.md:87 (~4.48 GiB to ~4.37 GiB) without correcting the copies in project memory. The underlying KB figure is consistent everywhere, so only the derived unit is wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Change all three occurrences to ~4.37 GiB, or cite 4,585,924 KB without a GiB conversion so the derived figure cannot drift again.

findings.problem: The entire deliverable under review -- local_files.py +93, main.py +85, tests/test_local_connector.py +128, tests/test_cli.py +99, tests/golden/test_golden_corpus.py +90 -- is committed under the message 'fix(S2-R-12, S2-R-13): remove host path from project memory; refuse sync on unreachable required root', which names neither S2-R-04, S2-R-03 nor S1-R-16 and describes a different pair of findings. 'git log -- src/lee_kb/connectors/local_files.py' gives no indication the nested-root work happened. This is a recurrence of S2-R-08, filed by the previous review against 4e9b989 for the same reason and still open.
findings.proposed_fix: Amend or annotate 19b8d4d before pushing so the message names all five findings, and record 'one commit message per finding set' as a standing rule in skills/documentation.md rather than a per-sprint correction.

findings.problem: No /usr/bin/time -v transcript was preserved for the post-repair run and no system validator executed the sync, so as delivered the headline -46.6% claim -- repeated as measured fact in context.md, result-review.md, sprint-plan.md and the customer-facing narrative -- rested on a single unpreserved worker observation. The figures themselves hold: an independent clean full re-sync by this reviewer reproduced them within 3% on every metric. The defect is evidence discipline, not accuracy.
findings.proposed_fix: Write the /usr/bin/time -v block, which contains no corpus content, to a file under evidence/ and cite it from the Performance section, or add a system validator that runs the timed sync, so the performance claim carries a record rather than an assertion.

correctness_and_failure_handling.justification: The three repairs are correct and independently reproduced: overlapping roots claim each file exactly once and deterministically; exactly one discovery pass per sync with cursor semantics, tombstone-not-purge and every counter preserved; the baseline gate fails on a simulated regression rather than merely passing today. Two failure-handling gaps remain, both about a candidate that reaches no counter -- a discovery-time read failure tombstones a live item and is misreported as a deletion, and a scoped sync loses overlap-region files silently.

governance_and_security.justification: Authorization is still evaluated before evidence assembly, receipts are one per released item, a refused request persists none, and governance.retrieve remains the only public evidence surface -- all exercised behaviourally rather than inferred from test names. No retrieval-path file changed in this slice. The only security-class finding is disclosure: absolute host paths remain in unpushed git history for a repository that is explicitly public, and one path shape is already published.

retrieval_quality.justification: No retrieval-path file changed (git diff 7e74e56..HEAD over governance.py, retrieval.py, repository.py and contracts.py is empty). Lexical, semantic and reranking providers remain replaceable behind LexicalRetriever; evidence bundles remain cited with source, sync and retrieval timestamps. The golden baseline is now an executable contract that demonstrably detects a one-place rank regression. The OR-matcher's measured worst case is unchanged and Open Question 5 remains open. No finding.

tests_and_documentation.justification: Repeated sync, changed source, deleted source, denied evidence and empty input are all covered, and the new nested-root, single-pass and baseline-contract tests are real regression guards verified by mutation. Documentation is where this slice is weakest: the customer-facing evidence report contradicts itself on the git-ignored counter and carries two statements the same edit invalidated, project memory repeats a wrong unit conversion three times, the commit message names the wrong findings, the original timing measurement preserved no artifact, and the golden-baseline per-question table is malformed and ungated.

scope.justification: The slice stayed inside its mandate: S2-R-04, S2-R-03 and S1-R-16 were repaired and nothing else in the retrieval path was touched. Office-format support and the curated golden benchmark remain explicitly deferred and are correctly reported as not implemented in result-review.md and context.md. No scope-drift finding.

residual_risks_open: Office-format support (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx) remains entirely unimplemented and open: FORMAT_HANDLERS covers Markdown and plain text only. The gap is sized at 39 files inside the 15 configured roots, and closing it needs both dependency approval and an include-pattern change on the affected roots -- the reviewer's re-derivation of discovery over all 15 real roots returned an empty unhandled-format histogram, confirming office files are excluded a step before any handler lookup. Deferred implementation, not deferred contract: DocumentType still enumerates the formats and the registry still accepts a handler without redesign.

The curated golden benchmark remains open: tests/golden/ runs a 20-question corpus generated from this repository's own documents plus three negative controls. S1-R-16 has made its recorded metrics an executable contract, which strengthens the harness but does not change what it measures -- it proves the evaluation framework, not Lee's real Chief of Staff questions against Employee Zero sources.

Existing projections will churn on the first post-repair sync: overlap-region items held under the parent root are diffed away as DELETED (tombstoned, so receipts stay resolvable) and re-created under the claiming root, producing a large deleted-plus-created count that is documented nowhere. Neither the re-measurement nor the reviewer's re-sync exercised this, because both deleted the database first.

A file's claiming root is decided before the git-ignore and handler checks, so in principle a claiming root that suppresses a file its parent would have kept removes it from the projection. On the real corpus this is benign -- document count is identical (1,213) with claiming enabled and bypassed -- but the decision order makes the divergence reachable.

health() labels two roots configured at the identical path as a nested pair ('alpha -> zulu'), telling an operator they are nested when they are duplicates. Claiming stays deterministic through the name tie-break.
The git-ignored counter is now a weaker signal of how much git-ignore is suppressing: it fell from 300 to 14 on the real corpus because the overlap region is no longer counted twice.

Sprint 1 advisories still carried at 19b8d4d: S1-R-12, S1-R-13, S1-R-14 (now the substrate _claiming_root sits on, since it compares resolved paths while the surrounding walk builds relatives from the unresolved one), S1-R-15, S1-R-17. Sprint 2 advisories S2-R-05 through S2-R-11 are all still present, including S2-R-06's 'ten of the 15 roots' count in the evidence report and S2-R-10's ruff deprecation warning, still emitted in the preserved step_05 record.

Git-ignore resolution is still delegated to whatever repository encloses a root, so the projection's contents depend on the enclosing checkout rather than sources.toml alone; 5 candidates on the real corpus remain git-ignore-unresolved and are indexed anyway, per the connector's count-it-don't-drop-it contract.
